assumptions: Numerical integration uses a variable-step, high-order integrator (explicit Runge-Kutta Dormand–Prince RK45 or similar) with tight tolerances (1e-9 abs, 1e-9 rel) unless stated otherwise.
Initial condition for time series is x(0)=0.1, x'(0)=0 for all runs; transients removed by discarding the first 200 forcing periods.
Time horizon per run is 400 forcing periods unless otherwise stated; sampling timestep for dense time series is at least 200 points per forcing period.
Poincaré sampling uses strobing at t_k = 2\pi k/\omega with interpolation to align integrator outputs to section times.
Bifurcation sweep uses 501 evenly spaced gamma values in [0.10,0.60], collecting 200 post-transient Poincaré points per gamma.

problem.original_text:
Nonlinear Dynamics: Duffing Oscillator (Chaos + Bifurcation + Poincaré)
Topic: ODEs, nonlinear dynamics, numerical integration, chaos diagnostics.

Problem:
Consider the forced, damped Duffing oscillator
  x'' + 2ζ x' + x + β x^3 = γ cos(ω t),
with parameters ζ = 0.15, β = 1, ω = 1. Treat γ as a control parameter.

Tasks (plot required in at least three distinct steps):
(a) Integrate the ODE numerically for γ ∈ {0.2, 0.3, 0.37, 0.45} over a long time horizon. Discard transients and plot the time series x(t). Use the plots to classify motion as periodic, quasi-periodic, or chaotic-looking.
(b) For the same γ values, plot phase portraits (x(t), x'(t)). Identify attractors (limit cycles vs complex/strange-attractor evidence) and explain how damping/forcing/nonlinearity affect geometry.
(c) Construct a Poincaré section by sampling (x, x') at times t_k = 2πk/ω. Plot the resulting points for each γ and compare the structure (single point, finite set, closed curve, fractal-like scatter).
(d) Sweep γ from 0.10 to 0.60 in small increments. For each γ, collect post-transient Poincaré samples and plot a bifurcation diagram of x-values vs γ. Locate period-doubling cascades and periodic windows.

Optional (still plot-heavy):
(e) Estimate the largest Lyapunov exponent λ(γ) numerically and plot λ vs γ to corroborate chaotic regimes.

Classify regimes (periodic, quasi-periodic, chaotic) and identify period-doubling cascades and windows.

classification.topic: Duffing oscillator; chaos; Poincaré section; bifurcation

steps.title: Convert to first-order system and state parameters
steps.explanation: Rewrite the second-order Duffing equation as a first-order system to prepare for numerical integration and variational equations for Lyapunov computation. State variables and parameters are explicit to ensure reproducibility and to derive the Jacobian used later.
checks: Dimensions: one second-order → two first-order variables

steps.title: Select integrator, tolerances, and initial condition
steps.explanation: Choose an adaptive, non-stiff integrator (RK45 Dormand–Prince) with tight tolerances to avoid numerical artifacts that mimic chaos. Fix initial conditions across γ for comparability and set sampling resolution to capture the forcing frequency.
checks: Ensure at least 200 samples per forcing period

steps.title: Integrate long trajectories and remove transient
steps.explanation: Integrate each γ for T_total = 400 forcing periods and discard the first 200 periods as transient to isolate asymptotic attractor behavior. This reduces contamination of Poincaré and spectral diagnostics by initial transient dynamics.
checks: Verify observable envelopes (e.g., max|x|) stabilize before using data

steps.title: Plot time series x(t) for selected γ and classify by spectral signature
steps.explanation: Plot post-transient x(t) densely to visually inspect periodicity, quasiperiodicity, or aperiodic irregularity. Use FFT of the same post-transient window as a quantitative check: discrete lines indicate periodic/quasi-periodic, broadband spectrum indicates chaos.
checks: Compute FFT peak sharpness and harmonic content to confirm visual classification
steps.notes: Expected: 0.2 periodic; 0.3 near period-doubling/quasi-periodic; 0.37 often chaotic; 0.45 often chaotic.

steps.title: Plot phase portraits (x,x') for each γ
steps.explanation: Plot post-transient (x,x') to observe geometric structure: closed limit cycles for periodic, smooth invariant curves for quasi-periodic tori projections, and complex filaments for chaotic attractors. Explain how damping contracts phase volume and nonlinearity creates folding that can produce complex geometry under forcing.
math_latex: \text{Limit cycle: closed curve; Torus: smooth curve(s); Chaos: fractal-like filament}
checks: Ensure attractor appears stationary over long windows; otherwise increase transient removal

steps.title: Construct Poincaré section by strobing at forcing period
steps.explanation: Sample the trajectory at t_k = k·2π/ω after the transient to form the stroboscopic map. The discrete set reveals period-n locking (finite set), invariant circles (quasi-periodic), or fractal scatter (chaos). Use interpolation to align sampling times with integrator output and avoid timing error.
checks: Interpolate integrator solution to exact t_k to prevent phase drift

steps.title: Sweep γ and build bifurcation diagram from Poincaré x-values
steps.explanation: For 501 γ values in [0.10,0.60], integrate and collect 200 post-transient Poincaré x-values per γ, plotting x versus γ. Period-doubling shows as branch splittings; chaotic bands appear as dense vertical scattering; periodic windows appear as isolated discrete branches.
checks: Refine γ resolution near suspected bifurcations to confirm structure

steps.title: Estimate largest Lyapunov exponent using variational equations
steps.explanation: Integrate the variational equation for a tangent vector alongside the trajectory, periodically renormalizing and accumulating growth factors (Benettin algorithm). A positive largest exponent confirms sensitive dependence on initial conditions; negative indicates convergence to stable periodic orbit.
checks: Check convergence by increasing integration time or varying initial perturbation magnitude
steps.notes: Use small perturbation (1e-8) and long integration (e.g., 2000 periods) for reliable estimates.

steps.title: Synthesize diagnostics to classify regimes and identify bifurcations
steps.explanation: Combine time series, FFT, phase portraits, Poincaré sets, bifurcation diagram, and Lyapunov estimates to assign regime labels and locate bifurcations. Cross-validation ensures classifications are not artifacts of numerical error or transient behavior.
checks: Cross-check Lyapunov sign with spectral and Poincaré evidence

steps.title: Perform numerical robustness checks and mention alternative methods
steps.explanation: Test sensitivity by rerunning selected γ with tighter tolerances and different integrators/initial conditions; verify that attractor geometry and diagnostics persist. Note alternative tools (AUTO, MATCONT) for continuation/bifurcation locus computation as complementary rigorous methods.

checks: Confirm qualitative invariance under tolerance, integrator, and IC changes

The bifurcation diagram over γ∈[0.10,0.60] should show period-doubling cascades to chaos with embedded periodic windows. Follow the provided numerical recipe and robustness checks to reproduce plots and Lyapunov estimates.

common_mistakes: Using too-large integrator tolerances or timestep, producing numerical chaos artifacts.
Insufficient transient removal that mixes transient dynamics with attractor sampling.
Too-coarse γ resolution in the sweep, missing narrow periodic windows or bifurcation points.
Failure to interpolate when strobing for Poincaré sections, causing phase misalignment.
Estimating Lyapunov exponents with too-short integration time or without reorthonormalization, giving unreliable signs.
